Context for the scope of the PUD: it zones the land for a data-centre technology park but leaves site and building plans to later approval, so it is not a data-centre building consent and is not used as a status observation.
us-midwest-iowa-ne-p4-farmington-ordinan.summary: The ordinance (scanned; page 1 read by rendering) adds 'PUD-1 – Farmington Technology Park' to the zoning code. Site, landscaping, lighting, grading, building, storm-water and utility plans and noise studies must be reviewed and approved by the City; the permitted use is 'Data Center Technology Park', with electric substations as accessory use; building setbacks are 250 feet from residential uses (including those south of 225th Street West) and 150 feet from non-residential uses.

us-midwest-iowa-ne-p4-farmington-pc-pack.summary: The staff report (packet pages 7-8) states that the Farmington Technology Park final plat approved on 18 November 2024 had not been recorded because of litigation and that the applicants ask to divide it into a 1st Addition (former Fountain Valley Golf Course) and a 2nd Addition (the Independent School District 192 property), identical to the approved plat. It lists Lot 1, Block 1, 1st Addition, 150.74 acres, 'northern portion of the data center campus'; Lot 2, Block 1, 1st Addition, 2.07 acres, to be deeded to the city for utility purposes; and Lot 1, Block 1, 2nd Addition, 185.54 acres, 'southern portion of data center campus', partly floodplain under a conservation easement. Recording the 1st Addition with the development contract would 'allow for some preliminary site work to commence'. The applications name MNLCO Farmington, LLC (2830 220th St W, former golf course, zoned MUCI) and, for parcels 07-00500-76-011 and 07-00500-76-012, the school district; counsel's letter of 30 March 2026 identifies MNLCO Farmington, LLC and MNLCO Farmington Two, LLC as 'Tract' and asks for a one-year recording extension for the 2nd Addition to 20 April 2027.
